articles.title: Deadly shooting near Paris investigated as 'crime of terrorism', minister says

articles.title: Mystery over source of Ebola infection in Nigeria fuels concern about spread of virus
articles.description:
Switzerland says patient is wife of Swiss diplomat and believed to have contracted virus while travelling in Uganda
Health officials across Africa are racing to determine how Nigeria’s first Ebola patient ⁠in more than a decade ⁠became infected, amid fears ​the outbreak could spread further after reaching a fourth African country.
The Swiss foreign ministry said on Friday the patient in Nigeria, the Ugandan-born wife of a Swiss diplomat based in Abuja, had not travelled to the Democratic Republic of ⁠Congo, where the outbreak was first detected in mid-May before spreading to Uganda, Kenya and now Nigeria. The woman was believed to have contracted Ebola while travelling with her husband in Uganda, the ministry added.
 Continue reading...

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton aims to extend career till early 2030s so he can race in African Grand Prix
articles.description:
41-year-old set on ‘dream to be able to race in Africa’

Rwanda to host despite criticism of human rights record

Lewis Hamilton has said he hopes to remain racing in Formula One until he can take part in the African Grand Prix which is set to take place in Rwanda in the 2030s. The seven-time world champion believes it is right that F1 is to hold a race there despite criticism of the country’s human rights record.
Last week F1 confirmed Rwanda was to host the African Grand Prix having concluded a 10-year agreement for the meeting on a purpose-built circuit, with the first race set for the early 2030s. It is lined up to be held on a circuit in Bugesera, 25 miles south of the capital, Kigali, which has yet to be constructed and marks a return to the African continent for the first time since it last held a race at Kyalami, South Africa in 1993.
 Continue reading...

articles.summary: ルイス・ハミルトンは、2030年代にルワンダで開催されるアフリカF1グランプリに出場するため、キャリアを延長する意向だ。人権問題の批判がある中、ルワンダでの開催は適切だと主張している。

articles.title: Controversial US-backed vaccine trial in African newborns halted

Hepatitis B study in Guinea-Bissau that was to be funded by CDC and that drew global backlash ‘will not move forward’
The US-backed hepatitis B vaccine trial in African newborns that drew global backlash was halted, the lead researcher said on Wednesday.
It was “now clear” that the study “will not move forward in Guinea-Bissau”, Frederik Schaltz-Buchholzer, a Danish researcher, wrote on LinkedIn, adding, “we were not given the necessary governmental approval.”

articles.title: Severely ill ICE detainees face imminent deportation to unknown African states, advocates say

Flights to third countries where the detainees have no ties are scheduled as early as Wednesday, relatives detail

Send us your questions about immigration and the midterms

Relatives of gravely ill detainees at two Florida immigration jails say authorities are about to deport their loved ones to unknown countries in Africa despite worsening medical conditions.

articles.title: Nigeria confirms Ebola case as outbreak spreads into western Africa
articles.description:
Case in Africa’s most populous country was detected in a woman who had travelled from Uganda
Nigeria has confirmed an Ebola case in its capital, Abuja, after a woman who arrived from Uganda tested positive for the virus, the health ministry said.
The woman began showing symptoms on 7 October and was admitted to a hospital in Abuja four days later, where she was later diagnosed with Ebola. It is unclear when she arrived in Nigeria, Africa’s most populous country.

articles.title: Alberta voters overwhelmingly reject plan to leave Canada in referendum
articles.description:
Result is a victory for prime minister Mark Carney and supporters of Canadian unity
Voters in Canada’s Alberta have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to begin the process of independence, delivering a decisive victory for supporters of Canadian unity and deepening divisions within the separatist movement.
With nearly 1.9m votes counted, roughly 76% people supported remaining in Canada, while 24% backed beginning a process toward separation, according to unofficial results from Elections Alberta.

articles.title: Madagascar launches safeguard investigation on certain confectionary
articles.description: On 12 October 2026, Madagascar notified the WTO’s Committee on Safeguards that it had initiated on 9 October 2026 a safeguard investigation on imports of sugar confectionary as well as chocolate and cocoa confectionary.
articles.titleJa: マダガスカル、特定の菓子類に対するセーフガード調査を開始
articles.summary: マダガスカルは2026年10月9日、砂糖菓子およびチョコレート・ココア菓子類の輸入に対するセーフガード調査を開始したことをWTOに通報した。

articles.title: WTO-ITC visit to Mogadishu supports Somalia's preparations for next phase of WTO accession
articles.description: The WTO and the International Trade Centre (ITC) conducted their first joint technical assistance activity in Mogadishu, Somalia, from 10 to 15 October to support the government's preparations for the second meeting of the Working Party on the accession of Somalia. Supported by the United Kingdom, the technical assistance event also included discussions on regional integration and the forthcoming Trade for Peace Somalia Initiative.
articles.titleJa: WTO-ITC、ソマリアのWTO加盟準備を支援するためモガディシュを訪問
articles.summary: WTOとITCは10月10-15日、ソマリアのモガディシュを訪問し、ソマリア政府のWTO加盟に向けた技術支援を行った。

articles.title: AI boom and trade resilience to Middle East crisis lift outlook, but gains to be uneven
articles.description: Global trade proved more resilient than expected in the first half of 2026 despite the disruption caused by the Middle East conflict, as supply chains adapted and strong investment in artificial intelligence provided a powerful boost to goods trade. However, the resilience was not uniform, with services trade and some regions more exposed to the effects of the conflict. WTO economists have therefore raised the forecast for merchandise trade growth in 2026 while lowering the outlook for services trade.
articles.titleJa: AIブームと中東危機への貿易回復力が景気見通しを押し上げるも、恩恵は不均一
articles.summary: 2026年上半期、グローバル貿易は中東紛争にもかかわらず回復力を示し、AI投資が物品貿易を押し上げた。しかし、サービス貿易や一部地域では影響が残り、恩恵は不均一。

articles.title: Services bodies spotlight Public Forum, remittance costs and development issues
articles.description: At meetings held from 7 to 9 October, the WTO Council for Trade in Services and the Committee on Trade in Financial Services commended the fruitful discussions on services trade at the 2026 Public Forum, continued discussions on transparency of measures regarding recognition of foreign service suppliers' qualifications, and exchanged views on how to reinvigorate the Council's work. Members also addressed how to facilitate digital payment systems and reduce the cost of remittances, help least-developed countries (LDCs) strengthen their participation in services trade, and various trade concerns.
articles.titleJa: サービス関連機関が公開フォーラム、送金コスト、開発問題に焦点を当てる
articles.summary: 10月7-9日の会議で、WTOサービス貿易理事会などは公開フォーラムでのサービス貿易議論を評価し、外国サービス提供者の資格認定、デジタル決済、送金コスト削減、LDCのサービス貿易参加支援について議論した。
